_comment: Major economic corridors, keyed by corridor id. The brief asks for forecasts
'across major economic corridors', so a corridor is a named object with a real
alignment rather than an abstraction over whatever hotspots happen to line up.
Like the authority table this is data: adding a corridor is an edit here, never
Waypoints are SAMPLING POINTS, not a route to drive. A forecast is produced per
waypoint and summarised for the corridor, so four to eight sparse points along
the real alignment is the right density.
Each waypoint names the place it sits on, and the loader carries the name into
`waypoint_names`: forty bare numbers are unreviewable, and the name is what
lets somebody check a number against a map before trusting a forecast built on
A corridor that crosses an international border names the foreign province
distinctly in `states` (e.g. 'Punjab (Pakistan)') and lists its countries as
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes in `countries`. Every corridor lists its countries,
including the domestic ones, so no country is assumed in Python.

ncr.name: National Capital Region
ncr.description: The Delhi conurbation and its satellite cities, the most densely monitored and most consistently polluted air shed in India.

delhi-mumbai.name: Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor
delhi-mumbai.description: India's largest industrial corridor, following the western dedicated freight line from the capital through Rajasthan and the Gujarat petrochemical belt to Mumbai.

punjab-haryana-stubble.name: Punjab-Haryana stubble belt
punjab-haryana-stubble.description: The Indo-Gangetic paddy belt whose post-harvest residue burning, carried south-east on the winter wind, is the single largest seasonal driver of Delhi's smog.

lahore-delhi-transboundary.name: Lahore-Delhi trans-boundary smoke corridor
lahore-delhi-transboundary.description: The two Punjabs are one paddy belt split by an international border. Residue burning around Lahore, Kasur and Sheikhupura in Pakistan's Punjab rides the same autumn north-westerly as India's own, crossing at Attari-Wagah and running down the Grand Trunk Road through Amritsar, Jalandhar and Ludhiana into the National Capital Region. The best-documented trans-boundary smog event in South Asia, and one no single-country monitoring network can see whole.

mumbai-pune.name: Mumbai-Pune industrial belt
mumbai-pune.description: The chemical, refining and manufacturing strip along the Mumbai-Pune expressway, where industrial emission and construction dust sit on top of a dense population.

chennai-bengaluru.name: Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor
chennai-bengaluru.description: The southern manufacturing and automotive corridor running inland from the Chennai port through Ranipet and Hosur to Bengaluru.

kolkata-durgapur.name: Kolkata-Asansol-Durgapur industrial belt
kolkata-durgapur.description: The lower Damodar valley coal, steel and thermal power belt, running north-west from Kolkata along the Grand Trunk Road to the Raniganj coalfield.

gauteng-emalahleni-middelburg.name: Johannesburg-eMalahleni-Middelburg (N12 and N4)
gauteng-emalahleni-middelburg.description: The road east from Johannesburg along the N12 and N4 into the Mpumalanga Highveld coal belt, where most of South Africa's coal-fired power stations sit inside the Highveld Priority Area declared under the Air Quality Act.

gauteng-durban-n3.name: Gauteng-Durban (N3)
gauteng-durban-n3.description: South Africa's main freight road, from Johannesburg over the Drakensberg escarpment and down through Pietermaritzburg to the port and south Durban industrial basin.

via-dutra.name: São Paulo-Rio de Janeiro (Via Dutra, BR-116)
via-dutra.description: Brazil's busiest industrial corridor, the Paraíba valley between its two largest cities, with the steel works at Volta Redonda and the aerospace and car plants of São José dos Campos along it.

br-163-arc-of-deforestation.name: Cuiabá-Santarém (BR-163)
br-163-arc-of-deforestation.description: The soy highway north from Cuiabá through the Mato Grosso grain towns into Pará, across the arc of deforestation where most of the Amazon's clearing fires burn each dry season.

br-364-rondonia.name: Porto Velho-Vilhena (BR-364)
br-364-rondonia.description: The highway that opened Rondônia to settlement, running south-east from Porto Velho through the cattle and clearing towns of the state to the Mato Grosso border.

manaus-porto-velho.name: Manaus-Porto Velho (BR-319)
manaus-porto-velho.description: The road south from Manaus through the interfluve forest to Humaitá and Porto Velho. Fire smoke from the southern Amazonas and Rondônia frontier reaches Manaus along it in the dry season.
